footer.aboutText: DevToolBox is a free, open-source collection of online developer tools. All processing happens in your browser — your data never leaves your device.

home.title: Free Online Developer Tools
home.subtitle: Fast, free, and privacy-friendly online tools for developers. All processing happens in your browser.
home.description: DevToolBox is your all-in-one developer toolkit, providing 10+ essential tools completely free. Whether you need to format JSON, encode Base64, convert timestamps, generate UUIDs, test regular expressions, parse cron expressions, decode JWT tokens, encode URLs, format SQL, or compare text differences — we've got you covered. All tools run entirely in your browser, ensuring your data stays private and secure. No server uploads, no API calls, no data collection. Our tools are optimized for speed and work offline once loaded. Perfect for frontend developers, backend engineers, DevOps professionals, and anyone who works with code daily. Bookmark this page and never search for scattered online tools again. DevToolBox supports both English and Chinese interfaces, serving developers worldwide. Start using any tool instantly — no registration, no login, no limits. Just open and use.

jsonFormatter.title: JSON Formatter & Validator
jsonFormatter.description: Format, beautify, minify, and validate JSON data instantly
jsonFormatter.seoContent: The JSON Formatter & Validator is an essential tool for developers working with JSON data. It allows you to instantly beautify minified JSON into a readable, indented format, or minify formatted JSON to reduce file size for production use. The built-in validator checks your JSON syntax in real-time and highlights errors with precise line and column numbers. Whether you're debugging API responses, configuring project files, or working with complex nested data structures, this tool handles it all. Features include configurable indentation (2 or 4 spaces), real-time syntax validation, and one-click formatting. All processing happens locally in your browser — your JSON data is never sent to any server. This makes it safe for working with sensitive API keys, credentials, and confidential data structures. The tool handles all valid JSON types including strings, numbers, objects, arrays, booleans, and null values.

base64.title: Base64 Encoder & Decoder
base64.description: Encode text to Base64 or decode Base64 to plain text
base64.dropFile: Click or drag file to upload
base64.seoContent: The Base64 Encoder & Decoder tool provides instant conversion between plain text and Base64 encoded strings. Base64 encoding is commonly used when you need to encode binary data as text for transmission over text-based protocols like email (MIME), or for embedding images directly in CSS, HTML, or JSON. This tool supports standard Base64 encoding as well as URL-safe Base64 variant which replaces + and / characters with - and _ for use in URLs and filenames. The file-to-Base64 feature allows you to convert any file to a Base64 string, useful for embedding small images, fonts, or other assets directly in code. All encoding and decoding happens entirely in your browser using the native TextEncoder/TextDecoder APIs, ensuring maximum performance and complete privacy of your data.

timestamp.title: Unix Timestamp Converter
timestamp.description: Convert between Unix timestamps and human-readable dates across timezones
timestamp.seoContent: The Unix Timestamp Converter is an indispensable tool for developers who need to work with Unix timestamps (also known as Epoch time). Unix time is the number of seconds (or milliseconds) that have elapsed since January 1, 1970 at 00:00:00 UTC. This tool provides real-time display of the current Unix timestamp, converting between Unix timestamps and human-readable dates, and showing the same moment in multiple timezones simultaneously. Features include automatic detection of seconds vs milliseconds timestamps, display in ISO 8601 and RFC 2822 formats, relative time display (e.g., '2 hours ago'), and multi-timezone comparison across UTC, Beijing, Tokyo, New York, and London. Perfect for debugging time-related issues in distributed systems, scheduling tasks, or converting timestamps from API responses.

uuid.title: UUID Generator
uuid.description: Generate random UUID v4 identifiers instantly
uuid.seoContent: The UUID Generator creates random Universally Unique Identifiers (UUIDs) following the version 4 (random) specification defined in RFC 4122. UUIDs are 128-bit values represented as hexadecimal strings in the format xxxxxxxx-xxxx-4xxx-yxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx, where y is one of [8, 9, a, b]. They are used extensively in software development for database primary keys, session identifiers, distributed system identifiers, and anywhere a unique value is needed without centralized coordination. This generator uses the cryptographically secure crypto.randomUUID() API when available, falling back to crypto.getRandomValues() for maximum randomness. Features include batch generation of 1-100 UUIDs at once, toggle between uppercase and lowercase, option to include or remove hyphens, and one-click copy of all generated values. All generation happens locally in your browser.

regex.title: Regex Tester
regex.description: Test and debug regular expressions with real-time matching
regex.seoContent: The Regex Tester is a powerful tool for writing, testing, and debugging regular expressions in real-time. Regular expressions (regex) are sequences of characters that define search patterns, widely used for text validation, search-and-replace operations, and data extraction. This tool provides instant visual feedback by highlighting all matches directly in the test string, making it easy to verify your regex patterns. Supported features include all standard flags (g for global, i for case-insensitive, m for multiline, s for dotAll), display of match groups and indices, match count, and support for named capture groups. Whether you're validating email formats, parsing log files, extracting data from structured text, or building complex validation rules, this tool helps you get your regex right the first time. All regex processing uses the native JavaScript RegExp engine.

cron.title: Cron Expression Parser
cron.description: Parse cron expressions and view upcoming execution times
cron.seoContent: The Cron Expression Parser helps developers understand and debug cron schedule expressions. Cron is a time-based job scheduler used in Unix-like operating systems, and is widely used in task scheduling for web applications, CI/CD pipelines, and server maintenance. This tool parses standard 5-field cron expressions (minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week) and provides a human-readable description of the schedule along with the next 5 upcoming execution times. Quick template buttons for common schedules (@hourly, @daily, @weekly, @monthly, @yearly) make it easy to get started. The parser supports all standard cron syntax including wildcards (*), ranges (1-5), lists (1,3,5), steps (*/5), and special characters. Perfect for DevOps engineers, system administrators, and developers working with scheduled tasks in Linux crontab, Kubernetes CronJobs, GitHub Actions, or any CI/CD configuration.

jwt.title: JWT Decoder
jwt.description: Decode and inspect JSON Web Tokens
jwt.subject: Subject
jwt.seoContent: The JWT Decoder tool helps developers inspect and understand JSON Web Tokens. JWTs are an open standard (RFC 7519) for securely transmitting information between parties as a JSON object. They are widely used for authentication and information exchange in modern web applications. This tool decodes a JWT into its three components — Header (algorithm and type), Payload (claims and data), and Signature — displaying each part in formatted JSON for easy reading. It automatically detects and displays standard claims like exp (expiration), iat (issued at), nbf (not before), sub (subject), iss (issuer), and aud (audience), with clear status indicators showing whether the token is valid, expired, or not yet active. The tool does NOT verify the signature (it's a decoder, not a validator), making it safe for inspecting any JWT without needing the secret key. All decoding happens locally in your browser.

urlEncoder.title: URL Encoder & Decoder
urlEncoder.description: Encode or decode URLs and parse URL components
urlEncoder.inputPlaceholder: Enter URL or text to encode/decode...
urlEncoder.seoContent: The URL Encoder & Decoder tool provides essential functionality for working with URLs. URL encoding (also known as percent-encoding) replaces special characters with %XX sequences to make URLs safe for transmission over the internet. This tool can encode text into URL-safe format, decode encoded URLs back to readable text, and parse complete URLs into their individual components (protocol, host, port, path, query parameters, and fragment). The URL parser feature breaks down any valid URL into its constituent parts, displaying query parameters as a key-value table for easy inspection. This is invaluable when debugging API endpoints, troubleshooting redirect issues, building URLs programmatically, or understanding complex query strings. All processing uses native JavaScript URL APIs for standards-compliant results. Everything runs in your browser with no server communication.

sqlFormatter.title: SQL Formatter
sqlFormatter.description: Format and beautify SQL queries for better readability
sqlFormatter.seoContent: The SQL Formatter helps developers write clean, readable SQL queries by automatically formatting and indenting your code. Well-formatted SQL is crucial for code review, debugging, and maintenance. This tool supports multiple SQL dialects including MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite, and SQL Server, ensuring proper formatting rules for each database system. Features include automatic indentation, keyword highlighting structure, SELECT/FROM/WHERE clause alignment, subquery indentation, and the ability to minify formatted SQL when you need compact queries. The formatter handles complex queries with nested subqueries, JOINs, CASE statements, window functions, and CTEs. Whether you're cleaning up auto-generated SQL, preparing queries for documentation, or making code reviews easier, this formatter delivers professional-looking results instantly. All formatting happens in your browser using the open-source sql-formatter library.

diffChecker.title: Text Diff Checker
diffChecker.description: Compare two texts and highlight the differences
diffChecker.seoContent: The Text Diff Checker is an essential tool for comparing two versions of text and identifying exactly what changed between them. This is invaluable for code review, document versioning, configuration comparison, and debugging. The tool displays differences with clear visual indicators — red highlighting for removed lines and green highlighting for added lines — making changes immediately obvious. Features include line-by-line comparison, statistics showing the count of added, removed, and unchanged lines, and side-by-side display for easy reference. Whether you're reviewing a colleague's code changes, comparing configuration files before and after an update, checking document revisions, or debugging subtle differences in similar files, this diff tool provides instant, clear results. All comparison processing uses the well-established diff library and runs entirely in your browser.
